title: A portfolio that grows with my work
text:
A listing automatically creates a collection of links from document metadata. Instead of manually rebuilding a project index each time I add work, I can add a QMD file to a folder and render the website. Quarto uses its title, description, and categories to create a new entry.
For a recruiter, this provides a quick way to browse my analytics and website work. For me, it keeps the portfolio organized as I add projects.

title: A portfolio that grows with my work
text:
How this listing is configured
listing:
  id: portfolio-projects
  contents: projects/*.qmd
  type: grid
  categories: true
  sort: "title"
  fields: [title, description, categories]
  filter-ui: true
  sort-ui: true
contents chooses the source documents; type: grid creates cards; categories groups the work; and the filter and sorting controls help visitors explore. A div with the matching ID positions the listing in the page.
Each source document includes front matter such as:
---
title: "Case 31: Member Experience Dashboard"
description: "A descriptive survey dashboard for credit union service insights."
categories: [Analytics, Customer research]
---

title: A portfolio that grows with my work
text:
How I would extend it
For future work, I can add a project file, write a concise description, and assign categories such as SEO, Analytics, or Content. Grid listings suit visual portfolios; table listings are useful for a compact research index; default listings work well for blog posts. The new item appears after the next render and publication.
Reference: Quarto Document Listings

section: CSS, SCSS, and HTML work together
text:
CSS, SCSS, and HTML work together
HTML provides structure: headings, paragraphs, navigation, images, and links. CSS controls how those elements look. SCSS extends CSS with variables and nesting; Quarto compiles the SCSS into browser-ready CSS during rendering.
In this project, Markdown becomes HTML. Classes on Quarto divs connect the content to reusable style rules. The site’s styles.scss contains Bootstrap theme variables in a scss:defaults section and custom rules in a scss:rules section.

title: Designing a clearer portfolio with CSS / SCSS
text:
Apply a theme in Quarto
The _quarto.yml file connects the stylesheet to the website:
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, styles.scss]
The dashboard declares the same theme under its own format: dashboard settings. That keeps the visual identity consistent across the website and dashboard.
